# Adjudication Task — Chapter 246

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃246화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|퀘스트
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|[성라대연]
 10|
 11|그 이상 무슨 말이 필요하겠습니까?
 12|
 13|거침없이 나아가십시오. 천하가 주목하는 이 연회의 우승자가 되어, 무림에 족적을 남기고 영광을 누리십시오!
 14|
 15|
 16|
 17|등급 : 초절정
 18|
 19|제한 : 진태경
 20|
 21|임무 : 성라대연 우승 (미완료)
 22|
 23|보상 : ???
 24|
 25|실패 : 화왕의 분노
 26|
 27|
 28|
 29|
 30|
 31|“…….”
 32|
 33|실패 시 받는 패널티에서 멈칫했다.
 34|
 35|아니, 성라대연 우승 못 할 수도 있지. 이걸로 화까지 내나.
 36|
 37|길길이 날뛸 적천강의 모습을 상상하니 내심 억울해진다.
 38|
 39|‘그것도 겨우 1년 가르쳐 놓고.’
 40|
 41|물론 나 같은 경우는 매우 특이 케이스긴 하다.
 42|
 43|그럼에도 굳이 퀘스트창으로도 알려 주는 걸 보니 적천강이 품는 기대감이 대단한 모양이었다.
 44|
 45|“태원진가의 진태경. 어디 있소?”
 46|
 47|“아, 여기요.”
 48|
 49|감독관의 말에 퀘스트창을 닫고 걸음을 옮겼다.
 50|
 51|한 걸음을 내디딜 때마다 사람들의 시선이 느껴지고 그와 함께 술렁이는 목소리가 귓가를 파고들었다.
 52|
 53|“태원진가의 진태경이라면…….”
 54|
 55|“산서잠룡?”
 56|
 57|“저 청년이 그자인가? 그, 화왕이 들인 제자라는.”
 58|
 59|“맞아. 확실해.”
 60|
 61|앞서 한 번 들어 본 노르웨이의 퉁명스러운 목소리도 들렸다.
 62|
 63|“흥. 믿는 구석이 있었군. 그래 봤자 허우대만 멀쩡한 약골이지만.”
 64|
 65|그렇게 사방에서 수군대는 말들을 흘려넘기고 절벽 앞에 섰다.
 66|
 67|뜻밖이라는 눈빛으로 나를 바라보던 감독관이 공손해진 어투로 입을 열었다.
 68|
 69|“깊이가 세 치(寸) 이상이면 합격. 그 밑으로는 불합격입니다.”
 70|
 71|“예.”
 72|
 73|세 치라면 약 10cm 정도의 길이.
 74|
 75|권법을 꾸준히 연마해 온 평범한 일류 고수라면 무난하게 합격할 수 있는 수준이다.
 76|
 77|하지만 막상 하려고 하니 긴장감이 몰려왔다.
 78|
 79|‘쓰읍. 도통 감이 안 잡히네.’
 80|
 81|정말 모르겠다. 여기에 세 치 깊이의 흔적을 남기려면 도대체 어느 정도의 힘을 줘야 하는지.
 82|
 83|가만히 절벽을 바라보고 있던 나는 도움말 기능을 사용하기로 마음먹었다.
 84|
 85|“저기, 감독관님.”
 86|
 87|“예?”
 88|
 89|“이거 어떻게든 깊이가 세 치 이상만 되면 합격인 거죠?”
 90|
 91|“그렇습니다. 단, 한 번 주먹이 떨어지면 그것으로 끝입니다.”
 92|
 93|“아, 그렇군요.”
 94|
 95|그렇다면야 쉽지. 고개를 끄덕인 나는 곧바로 절벽에 주먹을 댔다. 그리고 살짝 밀었다.
 96|
 97|푹! 투두두둑.
 98|
 99|두부처럼 부드럽게 갈라지는 절벽 표면. 부스러진 암석 쪼가리와 흙이 쏟아진다.
100|
101|나는 팔꿈치까지 박아 넣은 채 감독관을 바라봤다.
102|
103|“합격. 오케이?”
104|
105|“…….”
106|
107|감독관의 표정은 볼만했다.
108|
109|입을 떡 벌린 채 내 얼굴과 절벽에 박힌 팔을 번갈아 보던 그가 더듬거리는 목소리로 말했다.
110|
111|“어, 어떻게 하신 겁니까?”
112|
113|“밀었는데요.”
114|
115|“그러니까 어떻게…….”
116|
117|“그냥 힘줘서 밀었는데요.”
118|
119|“…….”
120|
121|“어쨌든 합격 맞죠? 주먹도 안 떨어졌고 깊이도 많이 들어갔으니까.”
122|
123|“그, 그게.”
124|
125|감독관의 동공이 흔들렸다.
126|
127|“자, 잘은 모르겠습니다. 지금까지 한 번도 이랬던 적이 없어서.”
128|
129|“그럼 됐네요. 지금부터 이러면 되니까.”
130|
131|“지, 진 소협. 죄송합니다만 조금 더 평범하게 안 되겠습니까? 저로서는 판단을 내리기가 좀…….”
132|
133|“평범하게요?”
134|
135|그게 잘 안 될 것 같아서 이렇게 한 거 아니야. 이 양반아.
136|
137|그냥 적당히 한 방 질러 봐야 하나, 고민하던 그때였다.
138|
139|“푸하하!”
140|
141|난데없이 튀어나온 폭소에 나를 포함한 모두의 고개가 저절로 돌아갔다.
142|
143|단연 눈에 띄는 거한, 노르웨이가 만면에 비웃음을 머금은 채 나를 바라보고 있었다.
144|
145|“튀고 싶어서 안달이 난 놈이로군.”
146|
147|난 턱을 긁적이며 대꾸했다.
148|
149|“딱히 그런 건 아니고. 근데 너는 왜 그렇게 시비를 못 걸어서 안달이 났냐?”
150|
151|“너?”
152|
153|“응. 너.”
154|
155|노르웨이의 마빡에 핏줄이 솟았다.
156|
157|“내 듣기로 화왕의 제자가 이제 겨우 약관을 넘겼다던데.”
158|
159|“스물둘이지. 다 컸어.”
160|
161|“나는 이립이다.”
162|
163|“서른? 나랑 비슷하네. 친구 할래?”
164|
165|“이 새파랗게 어린놈이 감히…….”
166|
167|존댓말 페티쉬라도 있는 건가.
168|
169|눈을 부릅뜬 채 한 걸음 나서는 그를 감독관이 만류했다.
170|
171|“자중하시오!”
172|
173|“자중은 염병할. 나한테 그렇게 말할 수 있는 사람은 사부님뿐이시다.”
174|
175|나는 느긋하게 팔짱을 끼며 물었다.
176|
177|“그래, 여태까지 그거 말하고 싶었나 본데. 네 사부님이 누군지 들어나 보자.”
178|
179|“해상왕(海上王).”
180|
181|해상왕이라면 혹시……?
182|
183|나는 경악에 찬 음성을 토해 냈다.
184|
185|“장보고!”
186|
187|“뭔 개소리냐! 사부님의 성함은 파륜이다! 해상왕 파륜!”
188|
189|“아, 하긴. 그럴 리가 없지.”
190|
191|실망한 나와는 달리 노르웨이의 입에서 흘러나온 이름은 대단한 파급력을 지니고 있었다.
192|
193|같은 조에 속한 지원자들과 감독관, 심지어 십여 장 떨어진 곳에서 심사를 진행 중이던 이들 사이에서도 웅성거림이 일었다.
194|
195|“해, 해상왕 파륜!”
196|
197|“장강수로맹(長江水路盟)의 맹주이자 십왕 중 한 명인 그 파륜?”
198|
199|“그럼 저 청년이 철수신룡이겠군. 어쩐지 화왕의 제자에게 겁도 없이 시비를 거나 싶더니.”
200|
201|“저쪽은 어떻게 되먹은 거야? 십왕의 제자가 둘씩이나…….”
202|
203|그런 반응에 노르웨이, 아니 철수신룡은 코웃음을 쳤다.
204|
205|대단한 사부를 둔 자랑스러움도 있겠지만, 자신의 실력에 대한 자부심이 그의 행동 하나하나에서 묻어 나왔다.
206|
207|‘뭐, 저 정도면 확실히 강하긴 하지.’
208|
209|십왕의 제자이니 어쩌면 당연한 일인가?
210|
211|심지어 나와 달리 저쪽은 어릴 때부터 해상왕 파륜의 지도를 받아 온 듯했다.
212|
213|장강수로맹이 얼마나 대단한 곳인지는 모르지만 무공에 영약에, 아낌없는 지원을 받았을 것이 분명하다.
214|
215|내가 팔짱을 낀 채 흥미롭게 바라보자 철수신룡이 피식 웃었다.
216|
217|“화왕의 제자라고 했나? 변방 무가 출신인 주제에 고작 일 년 가르침을 받았다고 어쭙잖게 나대지 마라.”
218|
219|아니 뭐, 틀린 말은 아니다. 산서성은 중원에서 떨어진 변방이고 태원진가도 변방의 무가가 맞다.
220|
221|그렇긴 한데…….
222|
223|“넌 해적이잖아. 너희 사부는 해적 두목이고.”
224|
225|“해적이라니! 네놈이 지금 장강수로맹을 모욕하는가! 우리는 강과 대해를 누비는 영웅들이다!”
226|
227|“그래. 근데 그걸 두 글자로 줄이면 해적 아니냐?”
228|
229|“놈! 무슨 망발이냐! 본 맹의 영웅들은 그따위 놈들과는 천지 차이다!”
230|
231|“천지 차이? 그럼 혹시 너네도 그 뭐야, 이상하게 생긴 열매 먹고 그러냐? 그거 먹으면 헤엄 못 치고 그래?”
232|
233|“노옴-!”
234|
235|“너는 놈놈 열매를 먹었구나.”
236|
237|우두두둑.
238|
239|철수신룡의 거대한 주먹에서 살벌한 소리가 들렸다.
240|
241|살기 어린 눈빛으로 나를 노려보던 녀석이 발을 내딛자, 감독관이 황급히 나와 그 사이를 가로막았다.
242|
243|“잠깐! 여기서 싸우면 실격……!”
244|
245|“비켜.”
246|
247|“헉!”
248|
249|규모가 워낙 크다 보니 심사를 통제하는 감독관도 하나같이 상당한 실력자들이다. 최소 초일류에서 절정까지.
250|
251|내가 속해 있는 조의 감독관은 초일류의 경지였지만, 철수신룡의 손이 어깨를 움켜쥐자 얼굴이 새하얗게 질렸다.
252|
253|“이, 이게 무슨.”
254|
255|“막을 필요 없다. 이쪽도 성라대연에서 우승하라는 사부님의 엄명을 받아서 말이야.”
256|
257|“그, 그럼…….”
258|
259|“안 싸워. 저 애송이에게 한 수 보여 주려는 것뿐이다.”
260|
261|감독관을 놓아준 철수신룡은 성큼성큼 절벽을 향해 걸어갔다. 그리고 망설임 없이 절벽을 향해 주먹을 밀어 넣었다.
262|
263|쩌저저적!
264|
265|단단한 암반을 부수며 팔뚝까지 꽂아 넣은 그가 나를 보며 혀를 찼다.
266|
267|“고작 이 정도다. 네가 한 것이.”
268|
269|처음 봤을 때부터 알고는 있었지만, 철수신룡은 매우 뛰어난 수준의 외공(外功)을 익힌 고수였다.
270|
271|저 정도의 덩치와 근력은 단순히 타고났다는 말로는 설명되지 않는다.
272|
273|무공. 그것도 극상승의 외가기공으로 단련된 것이 분명했다.
274|
275|오오……!”
276|
277|“과연 철수신룡!”
278|
279|가히 신력(神力)이라 부를 만한 힘에 탄성이 쏟아졌다.
280|
281|어지간한 절정 고수도 공력을 사용하지 않고서는 불가능한 일. 그러나 철수신룡은 마치 숨 쉬는 것처럼 쉽게 해냈다.
282|
283|그것도 보란 듯이 나보다 훨씬 깊은 구멍을 만들어 내면서.
284|
285|“화왕의 제자도 대단하긴 하지만, 역시 아직은 역부족인가?”
286|
287|“그럴 수 있지. 나이도 한참 어린 데다가 화왕이 제자로 들인지 일 년밖에 안 되지 않았나.”
288|
289|“산서잠룡도 나름대로 우승을 노리고 있었을 텐데…… 이번에는 어렵겠군.”
290|
291|주위 사람들이 뭐라 수군거리건 말건, 확실히 대단하긴 하다.
292|
293|이 정도면 사부가 누구인지를 떠나 무림 어디를 가도 큰소리칠 만한 고수임에는 이견이 없다.
294|
295|짝짝짝.
296|
297|“역시 힘이 장사네. 합격 축하한다.”
298|
299|“추하군. 억지로 태연한 척할 필요 없다.”
300|
301|“진심인데.”
302|
303|내 박수에 코웃음을 친 철수신룡이 감독관을 향해 고개를 돌렸다.
304|
305|연이어 벌어진 이변에 감독관은 얼이 빠져 있었다.
306|
307|“합격인가?”
308|
309|“아. 그, 그게…….”
310|
311|“상관없다. 어차피 이 정도로 끝낼 생각도 없었으니.”
312|
313|투두두둑.
314|
315|어이가 없을 정도로 쉽게 팔뚝을 빼낸 철수신룡이 주위를 둘러봤다.
316|
317|자신을 향한 사람들의 시선에서 강자를 바라보는 부러움과 질투, 그리고 절망감을 읽어 낸 그가 나를 향해 이빨을 드러냈다.
318|
319|“애송아, 파선권(破船拳)를 견식 하는 것을 영광으로 여겨라.”
320|
321|“파선권?”
322|
323|대답은 없었다. 그 대신 철수신룡의 전신에서 대해(大海)와도 같은 공력이 파도처럼 일어났다.
324|
325|곰보다 두꺼운 허리와 기둥 같은 팔이 뒤로 한껏 젖혀졌다. 그의 주먹에는 이미 강물처럼 푸른 공력이 넘실거리고 있었다.
326|
327|고오옹.
328|
329|주위의 공기가 요동친 다음 순간.
330|
331|콰아아아아앙!
332|
333|파선권.
334|
335|범선을 쪼개는 일 권이 절벽에 작렬했다.
336|
337|귀가 먹먹해지는 굉음과 함께 폭풍이 몰아쳤다. 쏟아지는 흙먼지와 암석의 파편에 사람들이 두 팔로 얼굴을 가리며 신음을 토해 냈다.
338|
339|“헉!”
340|
341|“크윽!”
342|
343|혼란스러운 상황 속.
344|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

After staring at it for a moment, I decided to use the Help function.

[P30]
“Excuse me, Supervisor.”

[P31]
“Yes?”

[P32]
“As long as I make the mark at least three Korean inches deep, I pass, right?”

[P33]
“That is correct. However, once your fist leaves the cliff, your attempt is over.”

[P34]
“Oh, I see.”

[P35]
*Well, that makes it easy.*

[P36]
I nodded, placed my fist against the cliff, and gave it a gentle push.

[P37]
Thump! Rumble-rumble-rumble!

[P38]
The cliff face split as softly as tofu. Fragments of rock and clumps of dirt came pouring down.

[P39]
With my arm buried up to the elbow, I looked at the supervisor.

[P40]
“I pass. Okay?”

[P41]
“……”

[P42]
The supervisor’s expression was a sight to behold.

[P43]
His mouth hanging open, he looked back and forth between my face and the arm embedded in the cliff. Then he stammered out a question.

[P44]
“H-How did you do that?”

[P45]
“I pushed.”

[P46]
“I mean, how did you…”

[P47]
“I just put some strength into it and pushed.”

[P48]
“……”

[P49]
“Anyway, I passed, right? My fist never left the cliff, and the hole is more than deep enough.”

[P50]
“W-Well…”

[P51]
The supervisor’s eyes wavered.

[P52]
“I-I’m not entirely sure. Nothing like this has ever happened before.”

[P53]
“Then it’s settled. This is how you handle it from now on.”

[P54]
“Y-Young Hero Jin, I’m sorry, but could you do it a little more normally? I’m finding it rather difficult to judge…”

[P55]
“Normally?”

[P56]
*I did it this way because I don’t think I can do it normally, you idiot.*

[P57]
I was wondering whether I should just throw a moderately powerful punch when—

[P58]
“Bwahahaha!”

[P59]
The sudden burst of laughter made everyone, myself included, turn toward it.

[P60]
Norway, the massive man who stood out from the crowd, was looking at me with open mockery.

[P61]
“You’re desperate to stand out, aren’t you?”

[P62]
I scratched my chin.

[P63]
“Not particularly. But why are you so desperate to pick a fight with me?”

[P64]
“You?”

[P65]
“Yeah. You.”

[P66]
A vein bulged on Norway’s forehead.

[P67]
“I heard the Fire King’s Disciple had only just passed the age of twenty.”

[P68]
“I’m twenty-two. I’m all grown up.”

[P69]
“I am thirty.”

[P70]
“Thirty? That’s pretty close to my age. Wanna be friends?”

[P71]
“How dare a fresh-faced brat like you…”

[P72]
*Does he have a fetish for honorific speech or something?*

[P73]
He glared and stepped forward, but the supervisor moved to stop him.

[P74]
“Control yourself!”

[P75]
“To hell with self-restraint. The only person who can speak to me like that is my Master.”

[P76]
I leisurely folded my arms.

[P77]
“So this is what you’ve been dying to tell us. Fine, let’s hear it. Who’s your Master?”

[P78]
“The Seafaring King.”

[P79]
*The Seafaring King? Could it be…?*

[P80]
I cried out in shock.

[P81]
“Jang Bogo!”[^1]

[P82]
“What the fuck are you talking about? My Master’s name is Pa Ryun! The Seafaring King, Pa Ryun!”

[P83]
“Oh. Right. Of course not.”

[P84]
Unlike me, who was disappointed, everyone else reacted strongly to the name that had just come out of Norway’s mouth.

[P85]
A stir swept through the applicants and the supervisor in our group. Even the people conducting examinations more than ten jang away began to murmur.

[P86]
“Th-The Seafaring King, Pa Ryun!”

[P87]
“Pa Ryun, the Alliance Leader of the Yangtze River Channel League and one of the Ten Kings?”

[P88]
“Then that young man must be the Iron-Water Divine Dragon. No wonder he dared to pick a fight with the Fire King’s Disciple.”

[P89]
“What is going on over there? Two disciples of the Ten Kings in the same group…”

[P90]
Norway—or rather, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon—snorted at their reactions.

[P91]
He was no doubt proud of his renowned Master, but confidence in his own abilities showed in his every action as well.

[P92]
*Well, he’s certainly strong enough to justify it.*

[P93]
Perhaps that was only natural for the Disciple of one of the Ten Kings.

[P94]
Unlike me, he also seemed to have trained under the Seafaring King, Pa Ryun, since childhood.

[P95]
I didn’t know exactly how powerful the Yangtze River Channel League was, but he had clearly received unstinting support—martial arts, elixirs, and everything else he could need.

[P96]
As I watched with my arms folded, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon gave a short laugh.

[P97]
“So you’re the Fire King’s Disciple? Don’t get cocky just because you come from some provincial martial family and received a mere year of instruction.”

[P98]
He wasn’t exactly wrong. Shanxi Province lay on the outskirts, far from the Central Plains, and the Jin Family of Taiyuan was indeed a provincial martial family.

[P99]
*That may be true, but…*

[P100]
“You’re a pirate. And your Master is a pirate chief.”

[P101]
“A pirate? How dare you insult the Yangtze River Channel League! We are heroes who roam the rivers and the open sea!”

[P102]
“Sure. But boil that down to one word and you get ‘pirate,’ don’t you?”

[P103]
“You insolent wretch! What kind of vile nonsense is that? The heroes of our League are worlds apart from such scum!”

[P104]
“Worlds apart? Do you guys eat those weird-looking fruits, too? The ones that make you unable to swim?”

[P105]
“You son of a—!”

[P106]
“You ate the Son-of-a-Bitch Fruit.”

[P107]
Crack-crack-crack.

[P108]
A vicious sound came from the Iron-Water Divine Dragon’s enormous fist.

[P109]
He glared at me with killing intent in his eyes and stepped forward. The supervisor hurriedly moved between us.

[P110]
“Wait! If you fight here, you’ll be disqualified—!”

[P111]
“Move.”

[P112]
“Gasp!”

[P113]
Given the scale of the Star-Array Grand Banquet, every supervisor overseeing the examinations was a formidable martial artist, ranging from the upper reaches of First Rate to Peak.

[P114]
The supervisor assigned to our group was at the upper reaches of First Rate, but the moment the Iron-Water Divine Dragon seized his shoulder, his face turned deathly pale.

[P115]
“W-What are you…”

[P116]
“You don’t need to stop me. My Master gave me strict orders to win the Star-Array Grand Banquet, after all.”

[P117]
“Th-Then…”

[P118]
“I’m not going to fight. I’m only going to show that brat one move.”

[P119]
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon released the supervisor and strode toward the cliff. Without the slightest hesitation, he pushed his fist into it.

[P120]
Craaaack!

[P121]
Shattering the solid rock, he drove his arm in up to the forearm. Then he looked at me and clicked his tongue.

[P122]
“This is all you accomplished.”

[P123]
I had known it from the moment I first saw him, but the Iron-Water Divine Dragon was a master of exceptionally advanced external martial arts.

[P124]
His size and strength couldn’t be explained by natural gifts alone.

[P125]
Martial arts had built that body—an external qigong technique of the highest order had tempered it.

[P126]
“Whoa…!”

[P127]
“As expected of the Iron-Water Divine Dragon!”

[P128]
Exclamations rang out at a feat of strength worthy of being called divine.

[P129]
Even an ordinary Peak master would have found it impossible without using internal energy. Yet the Iron-Water Divine Dragon had done it as easily as breathing.

[P130]
And, as if to make a point, he had created a hole far deeper than mine.

[P131]
“The Fire King’s Disciple is impressive too, but is he still outmatched?”

[P132]
“That’s understandable. He’s much younger, and it’s only been a year since the Fire King took him as his Disciple.”

[P133]
“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi must have been aiming to win as well, but… it looks like that’ll be difficult this time.”

[P134]
Whatever the people around me were whispering, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon was undeniably impressive.

[P135]
Regardless of who his Master was, no one could dispute that he was skilled enough to hold his head high anywhere in the Murim.

[P136]
Clap, clap, clap.

[P137]
“Now that’s some strength. Congratulations on passing.”

[P138]
“Pathetic. There’s no need to force yourself to act calm.”

[P139]
“I mean it.”

[P140]
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon snorted at my applause and turned toward the supervisor.

[P141]
After one unbelievable spectacle after another, the supervisor was still dazed.

[P142]
“Did I pass?”

[P143]
“Ah. W-Well…”

[P144]
“It doesn’t matter. I had no intention of stopping here anyway.”

[P145]
Rumble-rumble-rumble.

[P146]
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon pulled his arm free with absurd ease and looked around.

[P147]
Reading the envy, jealousy, and despair in the gazes fixed upon him—the looks people reserved for the strong—he bared his teeth at me.

[P148]
“Brat, consider it an honor to witness the Ship-Breaking Fist.”

[P149]
“The Ship-Breaking Fist?”

[P150]
He didn’t answer.

[P151]
Instead, internal energy as vast as the open sea surged in waves from his entire body.

[P152]
His waist was thicker than a bear’s, and his pillar-like arm drew all the way back. Blue internal energy like a flowing river already churned around his fist.

[P153]
Gooooong.

[P154]
The air around us trembled.

[P155]
Then—

[P156]
Kkwaaaang!

[P157]
The Ship-Breaking Fist.

[P158]
A single punch capable of splitting a sailing ship slammed into the cliff.

[P159]
A deafening boom rang out, followed by a violent gust. People groaned and raised both arms to shield their faces as dirt and shards of rock rained down.

[P160]
“Gasp!”

[P161]
“Urgh!”

[P162]
Amid the chaos, I stood perfectly still and watched without missing a thing.

[P163]
That was why, when the dust cloud finally settled, I could fully understand the cries of astonishment that erupted around me.

[P164]
*Wow…*

[P165]
The cliff stretched over a hundred jang in both height and width, a natural formation that had stood there for countless years.

[P166]
Now, a massive hole had appeared where none had existed before.

[P167]
No. It would be more accurate to call it a small cave.

[P168]
It was over ten jang across in every direction and five jang deep.

[P169]
“I-I can’t believe it.”

[P170]
“This is the Seafaring King’s unique martial art…!”

[P171]
An unmistakable thrill ran through the crowd.

[P172]
Everyone gathered here revered martial arts above all else and yearned to grow stronger.

[P173]
Their awestruck gazes converged on the martial artist who had just displayed a level of martial arts they couldn’t hope to approach.

[P174]
“Huff. Huff.”

[P175]
His broad back heaved. Muscles swollen almost to bursting rippled beneath his skin.

[P176]
After catching his breath for a while, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon turned around with a composed expression.

[P177]
A single short question slipped between his thick lips.

[P178]
“The result?”

[P179]
Only then did the supervisor come to his senses and barely manage to speak.

[P180]
“P-Passed. You passed.”

[P181]
“I see.”

[P182]
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon’s lips curled upward as his gaze swept over the crowd.

[P183]
The heat in his eyes had yet to fade. Finally, they stopped on my face.

[P184]
“Did you see that?”

[P185]
I gave a small nod.

[P186]
“What did you think?”

[P187]
“It was impressive.”

[P188]
“And?”

[P189]
“Hmm. Congratulations on passing.”

[P190]
“That’s all?”

[P191]
“What else? You want me to pat you on the ass?”

[P192]
Grind.

[P193]
Watching the Iron-Water Divine Dragon grind his teeth, I shook my head.

[P194]
*I told him it was impressive. What more does he want from me?*

[P195]
*What is he, a fucking child?*

[P196]
Maybe it was because he was a pirate, but he was as simpleminded as they came. The fact that he had poured out enough strength to leave himself breathless during the preliminaries was just as ridiculous.

[P197]
I clicked my tongue inwardly and spoke to the supervisor.

[P198]
“Let’s keep things moving. We’ve already wasted quite a bit of time.”

[P199]
“Ah, yes. Understood. Then, next…”

[P200]
I was turning away as the supervisor called the next name when the Iron-Water Divine Dragon spoke again.

[P201]
“Looking at you, I can tell what level the Fire Gate Clan is.”

[P202]
“What?”

[P203]
I stopped without meaning to. The Iron-Water Divine Dragon continued in a mocking voice.

[P204]
“Single-heir succession. No teaching to outsiders. It sounds grand, but in the end, aren’t you running away from me like a fucking dog with its tail between its legs?”

[P205]
“That’s your opinion.”

[P206]
“Is it only my opinion?”

[P207]
“What?”

[P208]
I suddenly looked around.

[P209]
Countless gazes surrounded the Iron-Water Divine Dragon and me.

[P210]
I could read the emotions in their eyes.

[P211]
*Disappointment. Contempt.*

[P212]
Beep.

[P213]
> **System**
>
> - People are whispering after seeing how terrified you look!
> - People are beginning to doubt the reputation of the **Fire Gate Clan**.
> - People are beginning to doubt the reputation of **Jeok Cheongang**.
> - **Fame** decreased by 18!
> - **Fame** decreased by 20!
> - **Fame** decreased…

[P214]
The System notifications pierced my ears.

[P215]
At that moment, I came to my senses as though waking from a long sleep.

[P216]
*So that’s how it is.*

[P217]
For a moment, I had forgotten.

[P218]
No—I had known, but I hadn’t truly understood what it meant.

[P219]
Even after the curtain had risen on the Star-Array Grand Banquet, this magnificent, dazzling stage where martial artists from all under heaven had gathered in one place…

[P220]
*This is the Central Plains. This is the world.*

[P221]
A world where everything was proven through strength alone.

[P222]
Winners and losers.

[P223]
A world divided into those two kinds of people.

[P224]
That was the Murim.

[P225]
“Hoo.”

[P226]
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon sneered when he saw me heave a sigh deep enough to sink the ground.

[P227]
“Looks like you’re finally ready to give it a try.”

[P228]
“Yeah. Thanks. That really woke me up.”

[P229]
“I heard you’re fairly skilled with a spear. I’ll graciously permit you to…”

[P230]
“You called it the Ship-Breaking Fist, right?”

[P231]
“Huh?”

[P232]
“It might be able to split a ship, but a cliff is beyond it.”

[P233]
Whoosh.

[P234]
One step.

[P235]
The distance of five jang vanished.

[P236]
By the time my foot touched the ground again, I had already passed the Iron-Water Divine Dragon.

[P237]
A belated cry of shock came from behind me.

[P238]
“You—!”

[P239]
Instead of answering, I looked up at the cliff before me.

[P240]
The fire dragon sleeping in my dantian awoke and surged through every limb and bone. Hundreds of acupoints grew scorching hot.

[P241]
“Jin Taekyung!”

[P242]
“You fucking weakling. Consider it an honor to witness the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.”

[P243]
Blue flames filled my vision.

[P244]
[^1]: Jang Bogo was a famed ninth-century Korean maritime commander and trader.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 246

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃246화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|퀘스트
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|[성라대연]
 10|
 11|그 이상 무슨 말이 필요하겠습니까?
 12|
 13|거침없이 나아가십시오. 천하가 주목하는 이 연회의 우승자가 되어, 무림에 족적을 남기고 영광을 누리십시오!
 14|
 15|
 16|
 17|등급 : 초절정
 18|
 19|제한 : 진태경
 20|
 21|임무 : 성라대연 우승 (미완료)
 22|
 23|보상 : ???
 24|
 25|실패 : 화왕의 분노
 26|
 27|
 28|
 29|
 30|
 31|“…….”
 32|
 33|실패 시 받는 패널티에서 멈칫했다.
 34|
 35|아니, 성라대연 우승 못 할 수도 있지. 이걸로 화까지 내나.
 36|
 37|길길이 날뛸 적천강의 모습을 상상하니 내심 억울해진다.
 38|
 39|‘그것도 겨우 1년 가르쳐 놓고.’
 40|
 41|물론 나 같은 경우는 매우 특이 케이스긴 하다.
 42|
 43|그럼에도 굳이 퀘스트창으로도 알려 주는 걸 보니 적천강이 품는 기대감이 대단한 모양이었다.
 44|
 45|“태원진가의 진태경. 어디 있소?”
 46|
 47|“아, 여기요.”
 48|
 49|감독관의 말에 퀘스트창을 닫고 걸음을 옮겼다.
 50|
 51|한 걸음을 내디딜 때마다 사람들의 시선이 느껴지고 그와 함께 술렁이는 목소리가 귓가를 파고들었다.
 52|
 53|“태원진가의 진태경이라면…….”
 54|
 55|“산서잠룡?”
 56|
 57|“저 청년이 그자인가? 그, 화왕이 들인 제자라는.”
 58|
 59|“맞아. 확실해.”
 60|
 61|앞서 한 번 들어 본 노르웨이의 퉁명스러운 목소리도 들렸다.
 62|
 63|“흥. 믿는 구석이 있었군. 그래 봤자 허우대만 멀쩡한 약골이지만.”
 64|
 65|그렇게 사방에서 수군대는 말들을 흘려넘기고 절벽 앞에 섰다.
 66|
 67|뜻밖이라는 눈빛으로 나를 바라보던 감독관이 공손해진 어투로 입을 열었다.
 68|
 69|“깊이가 세 치(寸) 이상이면 합격. 그 밑으로는 불합격입니다.”
 70|
 71|“예.”
 72|
 73|세 치라면 약 10cm 정도의 길이.
 74|
 75|권법을 꾸준히 연마해 온 평범한 일류 고수라면 무난하게 합격할 수 있는 수준이다.
 76|
 77|하지만 막상 하려고 하니 긴장감이 몰려왔다.
 78|
 79|‘쓰읍. 도통 감이 안 잡히네.’
 80|
 81|정말 모르겠다. 여기에 세 치 깊이의 흔적을 남기려면 도대체 어느 정도의 힘을 줘야 하는지.
 82|
 83|가만히 절벽을 바라보고 있던 나는 도움말 기능을 사용하기로 마음먹었다.
 84|
 85|“저기, 감독관님.”
 86|
 87|“예?”
 88|
 89|“이거 어떻게든 깊이가 세 치 이상만 되면 합격인 거죠?”
 90|
 91|“그렇습니다. 단, 한 번 주먹이 떨어지면 그것으로 끝입니다.”
 92|
 93|“아, 그렇군요.”
 94|
 95|그렇다면야 쉽지. 고개를 끄덕인 나는 곧바로 절벽에 주먹을 댔다. 그리고 살짝 밀었다.
 96|

I nodded, placed my fist against the cliff, and gave it a gentle push.

[P37]
Thump! Rumble-rumble-rumble!

[P38]
The cliff face split as softly as tofu. Fragments of rock and clumps of dirt came pouring down.

[P39]
With my arm buried up to the elbow, I looked at the supervisor.

[P40]
“I pass. Okay?”

[P41]
“……”

[P42]
The supervisor’s expression was a sight to behold.

[P43]
His mouth hanging open, he looked back and forth between my face and the arm embedded in the cliff. Then he stammered out a question.

[P44]
“H-How did you do that?”

[P45]
“I pushed.”

[P46]
“I mean, how did you…”

[P47]
“I just put some strength into it and pushed.”

[P48]
“……”

[P49]
“Anyway, I passed, right? My fist never left the cliff, and the hole is more than deep enough.”

[P50]
“W-Well…”

[P51]
The supervisor’s eyes wavered.

[P52]
“I-I’m not entirely sure. Nothing like this has ever happened before.”

[P53]
“Then it’s settled. This is how you handle it from now on.”

[P54]
“Y-Young Hero Jin, I’m sorry, but could you do it a little more normally? I’m finding it rather difficult to judge…”

[P55]
“Normally?”

[P56]
*I did it this way because I don’t think I can do it normally, you idiot.*

[P57]
I was wondering whether I should just throw a moderately powerful punch when—

[P58]
“Bwahahaha!”

[P59]
The sudden burst of laughter made everyone, myself included, turn toward it.

[P60]
Norway, the massive man who stood out from the crowd, was looking at me with open mockery.

[P61]
“You’re desperate to stand out, aren’t you?”

[P62]
I scratched my chin.

[P63]
“Not particularly. But why are you so desperate to pick a fight with me?”

[P64]
“You?”

[P65]
“Yeah. You.”

[P66]
A vein bulged on Norway’s forehead.

[P67]
“I heard the Fire King’s Disciple had only just passed the age of twenty.”

[P68]
“I’m twenty-two. I’m all grown up.”

[P69]
“I am thirty.”

[P70]
“Thirty? That’s pretty close to my age. Wanna be friends?”

[P71]
“How dare a fresh-faced brat like you…”

[P72]
*Does he have a fetish for honorific speech or something?*

[P73]
He glared and stepped forward, but the supervisor moved to stop him.

[P74]
“Control yourself!”

[P75]
“To hell with self-restraint. The only person who can speak to me like that is my Master.”

[P76]
I leisurely folded my arms.

[P77]
“So this is what you’ve been dying to tell us. Fine, let’s hear it. Who’s your Master?”

[P78]
“The Seafaring King.”

[P79]
*The Seafaring King? Could it be…?*

[P80]
I cried out in shock.

[P81]
“Jang Bogo!”[^1]

[P82]
“What the fuck are you talking about? My Master’s name is Pa Ryun! The Seafaring King, Pa Ryun!”

[P83]
“Oh. Right. Of course not.”

[P84]
Unlike me, who was disappointed, everyone else reacted strongly to the name that had just come out of Norway’s mouth.

[P85]
A stir swept through the applicants and the supervisor in our group. Even the people conducting examinations more than ten jang away began to murmur.

[P86]
“Th-The Seafaring King, Pa Ryun!”

[P87]
“Pa Ryun, the Alliance Leader of the Yangtze River Channel League and one of the Ten Kings?”

[P88]
“Then that young man must be the Iron-Water Divine Dragon. No wonder he dared to pick a fight with the Fire King’s Disciple.”

[P89]
“What is going on over there? Two disciples of the Ten Kings in the same group…”

[P90]
Norway—or rather, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon—snorted at their reactions.

[P91]
He was no doubt proud of his renowned Master, but confidence in his own abilities showed in his every action as well.

[P92]
*Well, he’s certainly strong enough to justify it.*

[P93]
Perhaps that was only natural for the Disciple of one of the Ten Kings.

[P94]
Unlike me, he also seemed to have trained under the Seafaring King, Pa Ryun, since childhood.

[P95]
I didn’t know exactly how powerful the Yangtze River Channel League was, but he had clearly received unstinting support—martial arts, elixirs, and everything else he could need.

[P96]
As I watched with my arms folded, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon gave a short laugh.

[P97]
“So you’re the Fire King’s Disciple? Don’t get cocky just because you come from some provincial martial family and received a mere year of instruction.”

[P98]
He wasn’t exactly wrong. Shanxi Province lay on the outskirts, far from the Central Plains, and the Jin Family of Taiyuan was indeed a provincial martial family.

[P99]
*That may be true, but…*

[P100]
“You’re a pirate. And your Master is a pirate chief.”

[P101]
“A pirate? How dare you insult the Yangtze River Channel League! We are heroes who roam the rivers and the open sea!”

[P102]
“Sure. But boil that down to one word and you get ‘pirate,’ don’t you?”

[P103]
“You insolent wretch! What kind of vile nonsense is that? The heroes of our League are worlds apart from such scum!”

[P104]
“Worlds apart? Do you guys eat those weird-looking fruits, too? The ones that make you unable to swim?”

[P105]
“You son of a—!”

[P106]
“You ate the Son-of-a-Bitch Fruit.”

[P107]
Crack-crack-crack.

[P108]
A vicious sound came from the Iron-Water Divine Dragon’s enormous fist.

[P109]
He glared at me with killing intent in his eyes and stepped forward. The supervisor hurriedly moved between us.

[P110]
“Wait! If you fight here, you’ll be disqualified—!”

[P111]
“Move.”

[P112]
“Gasp!”

[P113]
Given the scale of the Star-Array Grand Banquet, every supervisor overseeing the examinations was a formidable martial artist, ranging from the upper reaches of First Rate to Peak.

[P114]
The supervisor assigned to our group was at the upper reaches of First Rate, but the moment the Iron-Water Divine Dragon seized his shoulder, his face turned deathly pale.

[P115]
“W-What are you…”

[P116]
“You don’t need to stop me. My Master gave me strict orders to win the Star-Array Grand Banquet, after all.”

[P117]
“Th-Then…”

[P118]
“I’m not going to fight. I’m only going to show that brat one move.”

[P119]
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon released the supervisor and strode toward the cliff. Without the slightest hesitation, he pushed his fist into it.

[P120]
Craaaack!

[P121]
Shattering the solid rock, he drove his arm in up to the forearm. Then he looked at me and clicked his tongue.

[P122]
“This is all you accomplished.”

[P123]
I had known it from the moment I first saw him, but the Iron-Water Divine Dragon was a master of exceptionally advanced external martial arts.

[P124]
His size and strength couldn’t be explained by natural gifts alone.

[P125]
Martial arts had built that body—an external qigong technique of the highest order had tempered it.

[P126]
“Whoa…!”

[P127]
“As expected of the Iron-Water Divine Dragon!”

[P128]
Exclamations rang out at a feat of strength worthy of being called divine.

[P129]
Even an ordinary Peak master would have found it impossible without using internal energy. Yet the Iron-Water Divine Dragon had done it as easily as breathing.

[P130]
And, as if to make a point, he had created a hole far deeper than mine.

[P131]
“The Fire King’s Disciple is impressive too, but is he still outmatched?”

[P132]
“That’s understandable. He’s much younger, and it’s only been a year since the Fire King took him as his Disciple.”

[P133]
“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi must have been aiming to win as well, but… it looks like that’ll be difficult this time.”

[P134]
Whatever the people around me were whispering, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon was undeniably impressive.

[P135]
Regardless of who his Master was, no one could dispute that he was skilled enough to hold his head high anywhere in the Murim.

[P136]
Clap, clap, clap.

[P137]
“Now that’s some strength. Congratulations on passing.”

[P138]
“Pathetic. There’s no need to force yourself to act calm.”

[P139]
“I mean it.”

[P140]
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon snorted at my applause and turned toward the supervisor.

[P141]
After one unbelievable spectacle after another, the supervisor was still dazed.

[P142]
“Did I pass?”

[P143]
“Ah. W-Well…”

[P144]
“It doesn’t matter. I had no intention of stopping here anyway.”

[P145]
Rumble-rumble-rumble.

[P146]
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon pulled his arm free with absurd ease and looked around.

[P147]
Reading the envy, jealousy, and despair in the gazes fixed upon him—the looks people reserved for the strong—he bared his teeth at me.

[P148]
“Brat, consider it an honor to witness the Ship-Breaking Fist.”

[P149]
“The Ship-Breaking Fist?”

[P150]
He didn’t answer.

[P151]
Instead, internal energy as vast as the open sea surged in waves from his entire body.

[P152]
His waist was thicker than a bear’s, and his pillar-like arm drew all the way back. Blue internal energy like a flowing river already churned around his fist.

[P153]
Gooooong.

[P154]
The air around us trembled.

[P155]
Then—

[P156]
Kkwaaaang!

[P157]
The Ship-Breaking Fist.

[P158]
A single punch capable of splitting a sailing ship slammed into the cliff.

[P159]
A deafening boom rang out, followed by a violent gust. People groaned and raised both arms to shield their faces as dirt and shards of rock rained down.

[P160]
“Gasp!”

[P161]
“Urgh!”

[P162]
Amid the chaos, I stood perfectly still and watched without missing a thing.

[P163]
That was why, when the dust cloud finally settled, I could fully understand the cries of astonishment that erupted around me.

[P164]
*Wow…*

[P165]
The cliff stretched over a hundred jang in both height and width, a natural formation that had stood there for countless years.

[P166]
Now, a massive hole had appeared where none had existed before.

[P167]
No. It would be more accurate to call it a small cave.

[P168]
It was over ten jang across in every direction and five jang deep.

[P169]
“I-I can’t believe it.”

[P170]
“This is the Seafaring King’s unique martial art…!”

[P171]
An unmistakable thrill ran through the crowd.

[P172]
Everyone gathered here revered martial arts above all else and yearned to grow stronger.

[P173]
Their awestruck gazes converged on the martial artist who had just displayed a level of martial arts they couldn’t hope to approach.

[P174]
“Huff. Huff.”

[P175]
His broad back heaved. Muscles swollen almost to bursting rippled beneath his skin.

[P176]
After catching his breath for a while, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon turned around with a composed expression.

[P177]
A single short question slipped between his thick lips.

[P178]
“The result?”

[P179]
Only then did the supervisor come to his senses and barely manage to speak.

[P180]
“P-Passed. You passed.”

[P181]
“I see.”

[P182]
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon’s lips curled upward as his gaze swept over the crowd.

[P183]
The heat in his eyes had yet to fade. Finally, they stopped on my face.

[P184]
“Did you see that?”

[P185]
I gave a small nod.

[P186]
“What did you think?”

[P187]
“It was impressive.”

[P188]
“And?”

[P189]
“Hmm. Congratulations on passing.”

[P190]
“That’s all?”

[P191]
“What else? You want me to pat you on the ass?”

[P192]
Grind.

[P193]
Watching the Iron-Water Divine Dragon grind his teeth, I shook my head.

[P194]
*I told him it was impressive. What more does he want from me?*

[P195]
*What is he, a fucking child?*

[P196]
Maybe it was because he was a pirate, but he was as simpleminded as they came. The fact that he had poured out enough strength to leave himself breathless during the preliminaries was just as ridiculous.

[P197]
I clicked my tongue inwardly and spoke to the supervisor.

[P198]
“Let’s keep things moving. We’ve already wasted quite a bit of time.”

[P199]
“Ah, yes. Understood. Then, next…”

[P200]
I was turning away as the supervisor called the next name when the Iron-Water Divine Dragon spoke again.

[P201]
“Looking at you, I can tell what level the Fire Gate Clan is.”

[P202]
“What?”

[P203]
I stopped without meaning to. The Iron-Water Divine Dragon continued in a mocking voice.

[P204]
“Single-heir succession. No teaching to outsiders. It sounds grand, but in the end, aren’t you running away from me like a fucking dog with its tail between its legs?”

[P205]
“That’s your opinion.”

[P206]
“Is it only my opinion?”

[P207]
“What?”

[P208]
I suddenly looked around.

[P209]
Countless gazes surrounded the Iron-Water Divine Dragon and me.

[P210]
I could read the emotions in their eyes.

[P211]
*Disappointment. Contempt.*

[P212]
Beep.

[P213]
> **System**
>
> - People are whispering after seeing how terrified you look!
> - People are beginning to doubt the reputation of the **Fire Gate Clan**.
> - People are beginning to doubt the reputation of **Jeok Cheongang**.
> - **Fame** decreased by 18!
> - **Fame** decreased by 20!
> - **Fame** decreased…

[P214]
The System notifications pierced my ears.

[P215]
At that moment, I came to my senses as though waking from a long sleep.

[P216]
*So that’s how it is.*

[P217]
For a moment, I had forgotten.

[P218]
No—I had known, but I hadn’t truly understood what it meant.

[P219]
Even after the curtain had risen on the Star-Array Grand Banquet, this magnificent, dazzling stage where martial artists from all under heaven had gathered in one place…

[P220]
*This is the Central Plains. This is the world.*

[P221]
A world where everything was proven through strength alone.

[P222]
Winners and losers.

[P223]
A world divided into those two kinds of people.

[P224]
That was the Murim.

[P225]
“Hoo.”

[P226]
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon sneered when he saw me heave a sigh deep enough to sink the ground.

[P227]
“Looks like you’re finally ready to give it a try.”

[P228]
“Yeah. Thanks. That really woke me up.”

[P229]
“I heard you’re fairly skilled with a spear. I’ll graciously permit you to…”

[P230]
“You called it the Ship-Breaking Fist, right?”

[P231]
“Huh?”

[P232]
“It might be able to split a ship, but a cliff is beyond it.”

[P233]
Whoosh.

[P234]
One step.

[P235]
The distance of five jang vanished.

[P236]
By the time my foot touched the ground again, I had already passed the Iron-Water Divine Dragon.

[P237]
A belated cry of shock came from behind me.

[P238]
“You—!”

[P239]
Instead of answering, I looked up at the cliff before me.

[P240]
The fire dragon sleeping in my dantian awoke and surged through every limb and bone. Hundreds of acupoints grew scorching hot.

[P241]
“Jin Taekyung!”

[P242]
“You fucking weakling. Consider it an honor to witness the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.”

[P243]
Blue flames filled my vision.

[P244]
[^1]: Jang Bogo was a famed ninth-century Korean maritime commander and trader.

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
